1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 e6 3.e4 d5 4.e5.strategy: Takes space and hits the knight with tempo, but Black hits back by attacking the c3-knight. Usually a run of exchanges follows that leaves White with doubled c-pawns and Black's queen active on f6 with pressure on c3; the game is open, and each side must know the forcing play.
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 e6 3.e4 d5 4.e5.name: English Opening: Mikenas-Carls Variation
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 e6 3.e4 d5 4.e5.background: The most common continuation of the Mikėnas–Carls Variation is 3...d5 4.e5, known as the Flohr Variation.
